subject: zoology
question_text: The eggs of Ascaris are called 'mammillated eggs'. Justify.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.58, VSAQ 138). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The egg coat
lines: The egg of Ascaris lumbricoides is covered on
the outside by a protein coat.
This coat carries small rounded bumps called
papillae, so the surface of the egg looks
steps.why: The name comes from the outermost layer alone, so the answer has to reach that layer and describe what its surface looks like.
common_mistakes: Describing the shell as smooth. The outer protein coat is bumpy.
Writing that the bumps are inside the egg. They are on the outer coat.
steps.memory_tip: Mammillated means covered with small rounded bumps, and that is the outer protein coat.
steps.margin_note: Two lines: the coat, then the bumps on it.

steps.label: Justification

lines.text: Bumpy protein coat, so the egg is mammillated

lines: Because the outer coat is covered with these
rounded bumps, the egg is called a mammillated
steps.why: A 'justify' question is answered by joining the observed feature to the name, so the last sentence must contain both the bumps and the word mammillated.
common_mistakes: Repeating the definition without ever using the word mammillated.
Writing that the egg is mammillated because it is fertilised. The two are unrelated.
steps.memory_tip: Say the feature, then say the name it earns: bumps, so mammillated.
steps.margin_note: One closing sentence joining the bumps to the name.

insider_note: A justify question is scored on the join: the rippled protein coat and the word mammillated must appear in the same sentence.
